result.summary: Scope test independently verified, not assumed from ELIXIR-DEV's report. Read lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex in full (git diff main...HEAD -- lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex, 453 lines, new file, no prior version). Ran my own greps: `grep -n "Repo\.|Ecto\.|HTTPoison|Finch|Req\.|File\.|System\.|Logger\.|GenServer|gen_statem|Process\.|:erlang|send(|spawn|Task\.|Port\.|:httpc|:inet" lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex` -- zero hits except moduledoc prose describing the purity claim itself and `Node.t()`/`Edge.t()` type references, which resolve to this file's own nested `Letflow.Definitions.Graph.Node`/`.Edge` structs via Elixir's automatic nested-module aliasing, not the Erlang distribution `Node` module (no `Node.list`/`Node.connect`/`Node.spawn` calls present). Confirmed zero `alias`/`import`/`use` directives anywhere in the file (grep for `^\s*alias\s|^\s*import\s|^\s*use\s` -- no matches), so nothing is pulled in beyond fully-qualified Elixir/Erlang stdlib (Enum, Map, MapSet, Kernel) already visible in the source. Independently ran `mix xref graph --source lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex --format dot` (0 outgoing edges -- isolated node in the dot output) and `mix xref graph --sink lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex` (empty -- nothing yet depends on it), then `mix xref graph --format stats` project-wide: graph.ex does not appear in either the top-10-outgoing or top-10-incoming dependency lists (files with as few as 1 edge do appear), corroborating zero compile/runtime/export dependencies for this module. This matches ELIXIR-DEV's claim but was independently re-derived, not trusted. Module implements pure structural graph validation (8 CHK checks + DFS cycle detection) over plain structs (Node/Edge/Violation), taking already-typed input -- no Repo, no DB, no HTTP, no file I/O, no process/message-passing, no Logger, no clock read, no config/secret resolution. Not wired into the Plug router (router.ex has unrelated pre-existing dirty-tree changes, out of scope per this run's brief; mix xref --sink also confirms zero current callers). Not a migration (no priv/repo/migrations/*.exs in this diff). Not a lookup-by-ID handler, not response-shaping for a tenant entity, does not resolve any secret. Scope test result: NO tenant-data path touched. Per WF-02 Step 2c and security-invariants.md's applicability notes, this is out-of-scope -- INV-1/2/3/5 are stage-gated to S1/S4/S5 (not started) and independently not applicable here regardless; INV-4 (secrets) not applicable, no System.get_env/config/secret resolution in this file; INV-7 (SQL interpolation) not applicable, zero SQL of any kind; INV-8 (unhandled crashes on I/O paths) not applicable, zero external I/O for a crash to occur against, and the file's own `with ... else :error ->` patterns in build_adjacency/2 and check_isolated_nodes/1 are defensive rather than bare-matching. No deviation from the module's zero-I/O design contract found -- the full INV-1..INV-8 review was not required per Step 2c's shortcut.
